title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-08-15
summary: Weekly SRE digest covering incidents, SLO health, handoffs, and action items for the week of 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-15. Primary focus: remediation and follow-up from the 2026-08-12 cognitive-model-serving incident, tightening alert thresholds for bursty tail latency, and completing the runbook edits for cache warmup behavior.
incidents:
1) INC-2026-0812-01: degraded model-serving tail latency (2026-08-12 03:40 UTC).
- Impact: Intermittent 5xx spikes and elevated p99 latency for hosted API customers in us-west-2 for ~42 minutes. No data exfiltration.
- Root cause: cache eviction storm combined with a recent autoscaling policy tweak that delayed scaling decisions during short burst traffic.
- Mitigation: roll back autoscaling change (03:55 UTC), manual cache priming, throttled traffic for 12 minutes until p99 recovered.
- Postmortem: draft posted to Confluence, follow-up tasks assigned (see linked_artifacts).

2) INC-2026-0814-02: minor control-plane error causing failed model uploads for Dedicated customers (2026-08-14 18:10 UTC).
- Impact: ~7 customers experienced 503 errors for the upload endpoint for 20 minutes; uploads retried successfully.
- Root cause: transient database connection pool exhaustion during spike of CI-driven deployment automation tests.
- Mitigation: expanded connection pool and added backoff on the client side.
slo_updates:
- Hosting API availability SLO (99.95% monthly): Current month YTD 99.962% (on track).
- Model-serving latency p99 SLO (<= 900ms): This week average 870ms, but we saw spikes to ~2.4s during INC-2026-0812-01.
- Error budget burn: August to date ~0.3% consumed (majority due to INC-2026-0812-01).
- Action: add a temporary alert for 10-minute sustained p99 > 1.2s and add annual review ticket for autoscaler policy logic.
